evidence: Vulg. Ps. 9.18; Job 17.13; Ambr. in Psalm. 48.22 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The adjective īnfernus, lower, of the world below, made a noun in the Church’s Latin: Lewis & Short, “hell (eccl. Lat.)”. It is the everyday Church word for hell.
Hebrew Ge-Hinnom, a valley by Jerusalem where children were sacrificed to Moloch; in the Gospels the hell of fire (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Amic. 12: ad superōs … deōs potius quam ad īnferōs pervēnisse (Lewis & Short)
Ambr. hymn. Intende 23: excursus ūsque ad īnferōs
terms.comment: Classically the dead and the world below them (Lewis & Short, s.v. inferus). In Ambrose’s hymn Christ goes down ad īnferōs, to the dead, not to the hell of the damned.

phrases.english: “He was making hell,” he said, “for people who pry into deep things”

phrases.latin: ēgressus ejus ā Patre, regressus ejus ad Patrem, excursus ūsque ad īnferōs, recursus ad sēdem Deī
phrases.english: his going out from the Father, his return to the Father, his journey down to the dead, his way back to the throne of God
